extracted.intended_audience: research authors preparing Registered Report submissions to journals (Stage 1 and Stage 2)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on preparing Stage 1 and Stage 2 Registered Report manuscripts, obtaining in-principle acceptance (IPA), and meeting the methodological, reporting, and data-archiving standards required for publication. Covers required sections, statistical and methodological expectations, data-sharing, and policies on deviations, withdrawals, and incremental registrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 required sections and cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 submissions should include the sections outlined below and a brief cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are welcome to submit pre-submission enquiries but editors will not send manuscripts for in-depth review until a complete Stage 1 submission has been received. The Stage 1 cover letter should be a brief scientific case for consideration, refer to likely replication value (high-value replication studies are welcome), and include an anticipated timeline for completing the study if the initial submission is accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the research question(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will be asked to assess the importance of the research question(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may select only the most promising manuscripts for peer review in journals receiving high submission volumes; emphasize the scientific importance in the submission and cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic, rationale, and plausibility of proposed hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Introduction should review relevant literature that motivates the research question and provide a full description of experimental aims and hypotheses. Following IPA, the Introduction cannot be altered except to correct typographical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness and feasibility of methodology and analysis pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline (including statistical power analysis where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must include full descriptions of sample characteristics, objective inclusion/exclusion rules, and a proposed analysis pipeline. Where appropriate include statistical power analysis and justification of effect size estimates (see Neyman-Pearson and Bayesian-specific guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and methodological detail sufficient for exact replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the clarity and degree of methodological detail is sufficient to exactly replicate the proposed experimental procedures and analysis pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a description of experimental procedures in sufficient detail so another researcher could repeat the methodology exactly without further information. These procedures must be adhered to exactly in subsequent experiments or the Stage 2 manuscript can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specified outcome-neutral tests and quality checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors have pre-specified sufficient outcome-neutral tests for ensuring that the results obtained are able to test the stated hypotheses, including positive controls and quality checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full descriptions must be provided of any outcome-neutral criteria that must be met (e.g., absence of floor or ceiling effects, positive controls, other orthogonal quality checks). These are required to judge whether data can test the hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence requirement for In-Principle Acceptance (IPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: IPA indicates your article will be published as long as you successfully complete your study according to the pre-registered methods and submit an evidence-based interpretation of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to follow stated experimental procedures; any deviation, regardless of how minor it may seem, could lead to rejection at Stage 2. Substantial alterations after IPA require consultation with editors; minor changes may be permitted at editorial discretion and must be reported at Stage 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on post-IPA deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where the pre-registered protocol is altered after IPA due to unforeseen circumstances, consult the editors immediately and prior to completion of data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor changes may be permitted with IPA preserved and deviation reported in Stage 2. Substantial alterations require withdrawal and resubmission as a new Stage 1 if authors still wish to publish as a Registered Report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction content and immutability after IPA
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction should be a review of relevant literature that motivates the research question and a full description of aims and hypotheses; following IPA, the Introduction cannot be altered except for correction of typographical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any relevant literature that appeared after IPA should be covered in the Discussion at Stage 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: sample characteristics and inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Methods section must be a full description of proposed sample characteristics, including criteria for data inclusion and exclusion (e.g. outlier extraction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for objectively defining exclusion criteria due to technical errors or other reasons must be specified, including details of how and under what conditions data would be replaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: full procedural detail and adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of experimental procedures in sufficient detail to allow another researcher to repeat the methodology exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedures must be adhered to exactly in the subsequent experiments or any Stage 2 manuscript can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed analysis pipeline and transparency about contingencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed analysis pipeline, including all pre-processing steps, and a precise description of all planned analyses, including appropriate correction for multiple comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State any covariates or regressors. Where analysis decisions are contingent on the outcome of prior analyses, these contingencies must be specified and adhered to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of pre-planned vs exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Only pre-planned analyses can be reported in the main Results section of Stage 2 submissions; unplanned exploratory analyses will be admissible in a separate Results section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploratory analyses must be clearly justified, appropriately caveated, and reported in a separate section titled “Exploratory analyses”. Do not base conclusions entirely on statistically significant post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neyman-Pearson inference: power analysis and effect-size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies involving Neyman-Pearson inference must include a statistical power analysis. For frequentist analysis plans, the a priori power must be 0.9 or higher for all proposed hypothesis tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimated effect sizes should be justified with reference to existing literature, using the lowest available or meaningful estimate to offset publication bias. For highly uncertain effect sizes, variable sample size with pre-specified inspection points, appropriate Type I error correction for ‘peeking’, and a final stopping rule are permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bayesian hypothesis testing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods involving Bayesian hypothesis testing are encouraged and must specify the theory predictions so that a Bayes factor can be calculated (distribution and parameter choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify what distribution will represent theory predictions (e.g., uniform up to maximum, normal/half-normal, JZS/Cauchy with scaling). For Bayes factors, guarantee data collection until the Bayes factor is at least 6 times in favour of one hypothesis (or vice versa), or specify a justified maximum feasible sample size that would make inconclusive results informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome-neutral criteria descriptions (quality checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Full descriptions must be provided of any outcome-neutral criteria that must be met for successful testing of the stated hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include absence of floor/ceiling effects, positive controls, and other orthogonal quality checks that ensure the data are suitable to test hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and feasibility for completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a timeline for completion of the study and proposed resubmission date if Stage 1 review is successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts will generally be considered only for studies that are able to commence immediately; authors with alternative plans should contact the journal office. Extensions can be negotiated with the editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future-tense requirement for prospective methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Any description of prospective methods or analysis plans should be written in future tense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Stage 2, change future-tense descriptions to past tense and clearly mark any textual changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot data: inclusion and publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot Data (optional): Can be included to establish proof of concept or feasibility of proposed methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any pilot experiments will be published with the final manuscript and will be clearly distinguished from data obtained for the pre-registered experiment(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary registrations: evidence of no prior access
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary Registrations (optional): The journal welcomes submissions proposing secondary analyses of existing data sets, provided authors can supply sufficient evidence to confirm they have had no prior access to the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient evidence could be a letter from an independent gatekeeper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 submission contents and immutability of Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: The final manuscript should include the entirety of the Stage 1 submission, the raw data and laboratory logs, and the results and discussion. Apart from minor stylistic revisions, the Stage 1 submission cannot be altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any textual changes to the Introduction or Methods (e.g., typographical corrections) must be clearly marked. Relevant literature appearing after IPA should be discussed in the Discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision independence from result importance/novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are informed that editorial decisions will not be based on the perceived importance, novelty or conclusiveness of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may comment on importance/novelty on the record but such comments will not influence editorial decisions for Registered Reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 reviewer checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers at Stage 2 will be asked to decide: (a) if the data are able to test the proposed hypotheses by satisfying the approved outcome-neutral conditions; (b) if the Introduction, rationale and hypotheses are the same as approved at Stage 1; (c) if the authors adhered precisely to the registered experimental procedures; (d) if any unregistered post hoc analyses are justified, methodologically sound, and informative; (e) if authors’ conclusions are justified given the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The resubmission will most likely be considered by the same reviewers as Stage 1 but may be assessed by new reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data, materials, scripts, and lab log archiving
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data and any digital experimental materials must be made freely available in a public repository; raw data must be accompanied by guidance notes, analysis scripts, and other experimental materials to assist replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data files should be time-stamped to show they were collected after IPA. Other than preregistered data and pilot data evaluated in Stage 1, no data acquired prior to IPA may be added in Stage 2. Raw data should be archived in a repository (not merely submitted as supplementary material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and basic laboratory log requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must collectively certify in the resubmission Cover Letter that all non-pilot data was collected after the date of IPA. A basic laboratory log outlining the range of dates during which data collection took place must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lab log should be uploaded to the same public archive as the data, with a link provided in the resubmission Cover Letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol URL and embargo release
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript must contain the URL of the approved Stage 1 protocol on the Open Science Framework or other recognized repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the protocol was registered under a private embargo, the embargo must be released and the protocol made fully public at the point of Stage 2 submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of registered analyses and handling of flawed registered analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome of all registered analyses must be reported in the manuscript, except where a registered and approved analysis is subsequently shown to be logically flawed or unfounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such rare cases the authors, reviewers and editors must agree a collective error of judgment was made; the analysis would still be mentioned in Methods but could be omitted from Results with justification. Exact p-values and effect sizes must be reported for all inferential analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory/unregistered analyses handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional unregistered analyses are admissible in the final manuscript but must be clearly justified, appropriately caveated, and reported in a separate section titled 'Exploratory analyses'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid basing conclusions entirely on statistically significant post hoc analyses and must make clear which results were pre-registered vs exploratory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript withdrawal and withdrawn registrations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors with IPA may withdraw their manuscript following or during data collection; the journal will publicly record withdrawn registrations with authors, proposed title, the approved Stage 1 abstract, and brief reasons for failure to complete the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial withdrawals are not possible; withdrawing one planned experiment requires withdrawal of the entire paper. Studies not completed by the agreed Stage 2 submission deadline (6 months after receipt of the IPA, extendable) will be considered withdrawn and listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental registrations (adding experiments to approved submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can choose to add experiments to approved submissions; approved Stage 2 manuscripts will be accepted and authors can propose additional experiments for Stage 1 consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will seek to fast-track review of incremental experiments. If an incremented submission is rejected at either Stage, authors can publish the most recently approved version. Authors should contact editors for scenario-specific advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and repository guidance for IPA and differences from simple preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may publish their acceptance in principle in repositories (e.g., Center for Open Science, Zotero). Registered Reports and preregistration are not the same thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered Reports follow the two-stage workflow with IPA and integrated final article; preregistration is typically used to increase transparency (e.g., clinicaltrials.gov, PROSPERO) and has different conventions across subject areas.
